events.quote: Rule: subject, then verb, then object, then time at the end.
Right: Lina reads books at night. Wrong: Books reads Lina at night.
We use and to add an idea, but to show something different, and because to say why.

next_task.correct: The bus is cheap but it is slow.

events.quote: many + things we can count (many eggs), much + things we cannot count (much rice)
Rule: say "Can I have" + the thing + "please" when you ask for something.
Right: "Can I have a sandwich, please?" Wrong: "Bring sandwich."

next_task.correct: Can I have a coffee, please?

events.quote: The rule: for many verbs, add -ed when the action is finished in the past.
Right: Two days ago we cleaned the car. Wrong: Two days ago we clean the car.
some → positive sentences and polite requests ... any → negative sentences and questions
Rule: put am, is or are before going to, then the action word.
Right: We are going to swim tomorrow. Wrong: We going to swim tomorrow.

next_task.correct: I am going to study tonight.

events.quote: The rule: start a sentence with a capital letter and end it with a full stop.
Right: The bus is late. Wrong: the bus is late
Always, usually, sometimes and never come before the main verb, not at the end.
We use 'some' in positive sentences and polite requests ... We use 'any' in questions and negative sentences
The rule: use "Can I have ...?" or "I would like ...", and add please.
Right: Can I have some soup, please? Wrong: Give me some soup.

next_task.correct: Can I have a coffee, please?

events.quote: Rule: use many with things you can count, and much with things you can't count.
Right: How many pens are in your bag? Wrong: How much pens are in your bag?
The rule: after can, use the simple verb, with no -s and no -ing.
Right: She can dance. Wrong: She can dances.
For plans, use am / is / are + going to + base verb. Don't forget am, is or are!
The rule: start every sentence with a capital letter and end it with a full stop.
Right: Tom has a red bag. Wrong: tom has a red bag
1. Start every sentence with a capital letter. 2. Write the word I as a capital letter. 3. End the sentence with a full stop (.).

next_task.correct: the last time they agree on
the last time they agree on

events.quote: Irregular verbs have a special past form, with no -ed.
We say "She bought a red hat", not "She buyed".
The first time we talk about a thing, we use a or an. When we talk about it again, we use the, because now we both know which one.
we use a before a consonant sound (a book, a dog). We use an before a vowel sound
Words like always, usually, sometimes and never go before the main verb

next_task.correct: I always have breakfast at seven.

errors.W1: I have always breakfast at seven.

events.quote: Rule: start a sentence with a capital letter and end it with a full stop.
Right: "The dog walks." Wrong: "the dog walks"
Rule: use am with I, is with he, she or it, and are with you, we or they.
Right: You are funny. Wrong: You is funny.
